title: Use the integrated terminal
summary: Open the terminal, run a safe command, and hide the panel again.

steps.say: Click inside the VS Code window so it is in front.
hints: The title bar should end with Visual Studio Code.
Press Alt Tab to switch to it.
steps.why: The terminal shortcut only works when VS Code has focus.

steps.say: Press Control and the backtick key, left of the 1 key, to open the terminal.

checks.prompt: Is a terminal panel with a command prompt now open under the editor?

hints: On some keyboards the backtick key is elsewhere; open the Terminal menu and choose New Terminal instead.
Or open the Command Palette and run View: Toggle Terminal.
steps.why: The integrated terminal starts in your project folder, so commands act on it.

steps.say: Type dir and press Enter to list the files in this folder.

checks.prompt: Does the terminal show a list of file and folder names after a dir command?

hints: Click inside the terminal first if typing does nothing.
dir only reads; it does not change any files.
steps.why: Listing files is a safe first command and shows the terminal is in the right folder.

steps.say: Press Control and backtick again to hide the panel. The terminal keeps running.

checks.prompt: Is the terminal panel under the editor now hidden?

hints: The same key opens and closes it.
The trash can icon in the panel ends a terminal for good.
steps.why: Hiding the panel gives the editor more room without losing the terminal.
